llm.summary: The skill is focused on fal.ai through OOMOL, but its setup can execute an unverified remote installer if the CLI is missing.

dimensions.detail: The declared tool access is limited to Bash commands matching oo *, which is proportionate for a skill centered on the OOMOL CLI.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The first-time setup includes pipe-to-shell installer commands for macOS/Linux and Windows, allowing remote code from OOMOL installer URLs to run with the user's privileges without checksum or signature verification.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The trigger wording is broad for any fal.ai request, but the actual instructions remain bounded to fal.ai connector actions and require confirmation for write or destructive actions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill may lead to installing the oo CLI and signing into an OOMOL account, which are persistent local/account changes, but these are disclosed as one-time setup steps and raw fal.ai tokens are not handled by the user.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill purpose is coherent: operate fal.ai through the OOMOL oo CLI, with listed read, write, and destructive fal.ai actions.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review the first-time setup before installing. Prefer verifying the oo CLI installer through OOMOL's documented install guide or a signed/package-manager installation path, and do not let the agent run the installer automatically unless you trust that source. Once installed, the skill's fal.ai actions are reasonably scoped and write/destructive actions should require your explicit approval.
llm.findings:
[SC2] unexpected: The artifact does contain remote installer commands that pipe downloaded scripts directly into a shell; installing a required CLI is purpose-related, but this execution style is higher risk and under-verified.
[SQP-1] expected: The broad 'ANY fal.ai request' wording is present, but it is service-specific and paired with connector-only instructions and confirmation requirements for mutating actions.
